title: Korean Air Begins International Flights to Japan's Island Airport with A321neo
summary: Korean Air has launched twice-daily international service between Seoul Incheon (ICN) and Kobe (UKB), the first international flights at Kobe Airport. Operated with Airbus A321neo aircraft, the route aims to boost tourism and business travel to the Kansai region, linking Kobe to multiple East Asian cities and enhancing connectivity for Hyogo Prefecture and surrounding areas.
content:
KOBE-Korean Air (KE)has inaugurated its new Seoul Incheon (ICN) to Kobe (UKB) route, marking a historic milestone as the first international flight service at Kobe Airport. The twice-daily service strengthens Korean Air’s presence in Japan’s Kansai region.

The route operates using Korean Air’sAirbus A321neo aircraftwith 8 Prestige Class and 174 Economy Class seats, completing the journey in approximately two hours. This expansion comes as travel demand to Japan continues to rise, offering enhanced connectivity for travelers.

Korean Air celebrated the launch of its Seoul Incheon-Kobe route with commemorative events at bothSeoul Incheon International Airport (ICN)and Kobe Airport (UKB) on April 18. As the first Korean flag carrier on this route, Korean Air has established a twice-daily service with morning and afternoon departures:

This new route demonstrates Korean Air’s commitment to expanding its network in response to increasing travel demand to Japan. Further, the service not only enhances passenger convenience but also provides travelers with greater flexibility when visiting Japan’s culturally rich Kansai region.

Kobe Airport, which opened in 2006, previously handled only domestic flights until this recent expansion to international services. A ceremony celebrating the arrival of the first international flight was held at the new terminal building, with Kobe City Mayor Hisamoto Kizo expressing optimism about Kobe’s new potential as an international city.

The airport now connects Kobe to five cities across South Korea,China, and Taiwan, with40 round-trip flights scheduled weekly. Further, Korean Air’s regional manager for Japan expressed delight that the airline could help introduce Kobe’s charm to people in South Korea.

The first international charter flight to arrive at the airport came from Taipei, Taiwan, with passengers receiving a warm welcome from airport officials bearing commemorative items. This international expansion is expected to significantly increase foreign tourism and business travel to Hyogo Prefecture.

*Excluding Friday, April 18 and Tuesday, April 22.

**Also available on Friday, April 18.***Service will begin on April 21 (Monday), with service also available on April 19 (Saturday) and 26 (Saturday).

The introduction of international flights at Kobe Airport represents a substantial economic opportunity for the entireKansai region. With its strategic location near Osaka, Kyoto, and Nara, Kobe now serves as another gateway for international travelers exploring western Japan.

Tourism officials expect the new flight services to boost visitor numbers to popular attractions throughout Hyogo Prefecture, including Kobe’s famous Harborland, Arima Onsen, and Himeji Castle. The increased accessibility is particularly timely as Japan continues to experience a post-pandemic tourism recovery.

Business travelers will also benefit from more direct access to Kobe’s commercial district, home to numerous international corporations and Japan’s sixth-largest container port. This connectivity enhancement supports Kobe’s position as a significant economic hub in western Japan.

## Route launch

KOBE — Korean Air (KE) has inaugurated its new Seoul Incheon (ICN) to Kobe (UKB) route, marking a historic milestone as the first international flight service at Kobe Airport. The twice-daily service strengthens Korean Air’s presence in Japan’s Kansai region.

## Service details

- Aircraft: Airbus A321neo
- Cabin configuration: 8 Prestige Class and 174 Economy Class seats
- Flight time: Approximately two hours
- Frequency: Twice daily, with morning and afternoon departures
- This expansion comes as travel demand to Japan continues to rise, offering enhanced connectivity for travelers.

## Inauguration

Korean Air celebrated the launch of its Seoul Incheon–Kobe route with commemorative events at both Seoul Incheon International Airport (ICN) and Kobe Airport (UKB) on April 18. As the first Korean flag carrier on this route, Korean Air has established a twice-daily service with morning and afternoon departures.

Kobe Airport, which opened in 2006, previously handled only domestic flights until this recent expansion to international services. A ceremony celebrating the arrival of the first international flight was held at the new terminal building, with Kobe City Mayor Hisamoto Kizo expressing optimism about Kobe’s new potential as an international city.

The first international charter flight to arrive at the airport came from Taipei, Taiwan, with passengers receiving a warm welcome from airport officials bearing commemorative items.

## Connectivity and schedule

- The airport now connects Kobe to five cities across South Korea, China, and Taiwan.
- There are 40 round-trip flights scheduled weekly.
- Korean Air’s regional manager for Japan expressed delight that the airline could help introduce Kobe’s charm to people in South Korea.

## Economic and tourism impact

The introduction of international flights at Kobe Airport represents a substantial economic opportunity for the entire Kansai region. With its strategic location near Osaka, Kyoto, and Nara, Kobe now serves as another gateway for international travelers exploring western Japan.

Tourism officials expect the new flight services to boost visitor numbers to popular attractions throughout Hyogo Prefecture, including:

- Kobe’s famous Harborland
- Arima Onsen
- Himeji Castle

The increased accessibility is particularly timely as Japan continues to experience a post-pandemic tourism recovery.

Business travelers will also benefit from more direct access to Kobe’s commercial district, home to numerous international corporations and Japan’s sixth-largest container port. This connectivity enhancement supports Kobe’s position as a significant economic hub in western Japan.

## Notes

- Excluding Friday, April 18 and Tuesday, April 22.
- Also available on Friday, April 18.
- Service will begin on April 21 (Monday), with service also available on April 19 (Saturday) and 26 (Saturday).
